item.title: Saudi Arabia to invest $7 bn in theme parks near Paris: French presidency
item.description:
France and Saudi Arabia on Monday signed a memorandum of understanding for a six-billion-euro ($7 billion) Saudi investment to create three theme parks near Paris, including one likely to be manga-themed, the office of the French president said.

The French presidency's Elysee Palace said the agreement for the "colossal" project was signed during a two-day visit to France by Saudi Arabia's de facto ruler, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

item.title: France, Saudi Arabia agree on €6 billion Dragon Ball Z theme park project near Paris
item.description:
PARIS, Aug 24 (Reuters) - France and Saudi Arabia have agreed to build a €6 billion ($7 billion) manga-themed amusement park near Paris, the Elysee Palace said on Monday during a visit by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to the French capital.

The project, inspired by the world of the hit Japanese manga and anime franchise Dragon Ball Z, will be built near Cergy-Pontoise, northwest of Paris, and is expected to create around 22,000 jobs, the Elysee said.

item.title: Israeli fire kills two young children in Gaza, medics say
item.description:
CAIRO, Aug 24 (Reuters) - Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed two young children and at least two other Palestinians in the Gaza Strip on Monday, health officials in the territory said.

Medics and relatives said 10-year-old Amal Abu Khater was hit by a bullet in her back while she was eating inside her family's tent in the enclave's southern city of Khan Younis. The fire came from Israeli forces to the east, they added.

The Israeli military said it was not aware of any incident involving a 10-year-old girl.

item.title: US removes Syria's designation as State Sponsor of Terrorism
item.description:
Aug 24 (Reuters) - The U.S. State Department on Monday removed Syria from its list of State Sponsors of Terrorism, according to a notification from the Treasury, in a move that was first announced earlier this year pending a review by Congress.

(Reporting by Katharine Jackson and Costas Pitas; Editing by Daphne Psaledakis)

item.title: Stocks, oil slip ahead of US threat of economic war against Iran
item.description:
Oil prices eased after strong gains last week while stock markets mostly faltered on Monday as investors awaited details of a US plan to impose massive economic pressure on Iran to end the Middle East war.

Wednesday's earnings report from chip giant Nvidia and Thursday's opening of the annual gathering of central bankers in Jackson Hole were also adding to caution on stock markets.   

In New York, the Dow was trading higher at late-morning trading, but the wider S&P 500 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq were lower.

item.title: Explainer-What are Iran's options to escalate further in face of US economic threats?
item.description:
LONDON, Aug 24 - U.S. threats to impose "the toughest sanctions in history" to force Iran to buckle to its demands after nearly six months of war have raised the prospect of a new round of escalation in the Gulf.

How could Iran respond to the economic pressure?

CAN IRAN STOP MORE OIL GETTING OUT OF THE MIDDLE EAST?

Mohsen Rezaei, the former Revolutionary Guards chief and secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, has already threatened to shut down oil exports — one of Tehran's main strategic approaches since the war began on February 28.

item.title: US announces expansion of sanctions in 'economic onslaught' on Iran
item.description:
By David Lawder and Humeyra Pamuk

WASHINGTON, Aug 24 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump's administration on Monday announced an expansion of secondary sanctions it can impose on entities and countries that maintain business ties with Iran around the world as Washington significantly ratchets up economic pressure on Tehran with the war nearing its 6-month mark.
